decisions.decision: src/lib/session.ts exports a factory function (createSessionService(secret)) returning { create, verify, destroy }, instantiated once as the `session` singleton — not three standalone exported functions (the plan's literal text) and not a class requiring `new`
decisions.rationale: User dislikes scattered util-function exports but also dislikes class-instantiation ceremony; a parameterized factory groups the three under one cohesive name while keeping the secret an injected parameter rather than each function reaching into process.env directly

decisions.decision: ADR tech/0016 added: multi-param (2+) declared functions/arrows/methods take one destructured object parameter instead of positional args, enforced via 5 no-restricted-syntax selectors in eslint.config.mjs. Exempts (a) function/arrow expressions passed inline as a call/new argument (their arity is dictated by the API they're passed to — array callbacks, Promise executor, forwardRef, event handlers) and (b) object methods faking a fixed third-party interface shape (documented via eslint-disable-next-line, not a selector) — e.g. mocks of next/headers' cookies().set(name, value, options).
decisions.rationale: User flagged positional multi-arg functions as a readability problem at call sites; scoped narrowly after discussion to avoid breaking idiomatic callback signatures this project doesn't control

context_notes: Executing phase 01 wave-by-wave via gsd-executor agents in git worktree isolation (isolation="worktree"), one plan per wave since waves 10-15 each have exactly one plan with a linear dependency chain. Pattern per wave: capture EXPECTED_BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD) and a WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST, dispatch Agent(subagent_type="gsd-executor", isolation="worktree"), then record+cleanup-wave to merge. IMPORTANT: the harness sometimes auto-merges the worktree back to master on its own (saw this for 01-10) and sometimes doesn't (01-11 needed an explicit worktree.cleanup-wave call) — always check `git log --oneline -3` after an executor returns before assuming cleanup-wave is needed. Both times, cleanup-wave (or the harness) left a stray .claude/worktrees/<agent-id>/ directory and a worktree-agent-<id> branch behind after a successful merge — always `rm -rf` the directory and `git branch -D` the branch as a follow-up, they are not cleaned up automatically. Also: local master must be pushed to origin before dispatching a new worktree-isolated wave, or the harness's worktree forks from a stale origin/HEAD and the worktree_branch_check guard HALTs with exit 42 (base mismatch) — push after every wave's merge, not just at the end. Blocking checkpoint:decision tasks (plan 01-10 Task 1, plan 01-11 Task 1) were resolved via AskUserQuestion up front and passed into the executor's dispatch prompt as a pre-resolved decision (with instruction not to re-prompt), rather than letting the executor run to the checkpoint and pause — saves a wasted worktree round-trip since the orchestrator already has full plan context to present the decision faithfully.
